# Disagreement Log — Didache Chapter 16

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Didache 16 — Eschatological Warning and the Coming of the Lord
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA

---

## Summary
Total disagreements: 7

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.1: "let your loins not be ungirded" — idiomatic rendering

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "let your loins not be ungirded" |
| LOGOS | "do not let your belts be loosened" |
| PNEUMA | "keep your belts buckled" |

**Issue:** The idiom "loins girded" (cf. Ex 12:11; Luke 12:35) = dressed and ready for action. EMET's literalness is opaque in modern English.
**Ruling:** "Do not let your belts be loosened" (LOGOS) adopted. Clear and retains the metaphorical image.

---

## Disagreement 2 — v.2: τελειωθῆτε — "made perfect" vs. "hold on"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "unless you are made perfect at the last time" |
| LOGOS | "unless you are made perfect at the very end" |
| PNEUMA | "if you don't hold on to the very end" |

**Issue:** τελειωθῆτε = aorist passive subjunctive of τελειόω = to be made complete/perfect. This is eschatological completion — the full realization of faith. PNEUMA's "hold on" loses the passive (God makes perfect) and misses the τέλος (end/completion) resonance.
**Ruling:** "Unless you are made perfect at the very end" (LOGOS) adopted.

---

## Disagreement 3 — v.3: "love will be turned into hatred" — present passive

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "love will be turned into hatred" |
| LOGOS | "love will be turned into hate" |
| PNEUMA | "love will become hate" |

**Issue:** Minor. "Hatred" vs. "hate" — both work. "Turned into" preserves the passive construction (something acts upon love to reverse it).
**Ruling:** "Love will be turned into hate" (LOGOS) adopted. "Hate" is more natural; "turned into" preserves the passive.

---

## Disagreement 4 — v.4: κοσμοπλάνης — "world-deceiver"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "world-deceiver" |
| LOGOS | "world-deceiver" |
| PNEUMA | "world-deceiver" |

**Issue:** Unanimous. This unique compound is the Didache's term for the end-times deceiver. All agents agree: "world-deceiver."
**Ruling:** "World-deceiver" — unanimous.

---

## Disagreement 5 — v.5: ὑπ᾽ αὐτῆς τῆς κατάρας — the most debated phrase

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "saved by the Curse itself" |
| LOGOS | "saved by the Accursed One himself" |
| PNEUMA | "saved by the One who bore the curse" |

**Issue:** This phrase is genuinely difficult. Three readings:
- **Literal**: "by the curse itself" — the fire of testing paradoxically saves (purification?)
- **Christological**: "by the Accursed One himself" = Christ who became a curse (Gal 3:13)
- **Temporal**: "despite the curse" — faith survives even through the accursed time

LOGOS's reading links to Gal 3:13 (Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, having become a curse for us) and is the most theologically coherent in context. The emphatic αὐτῆς supports "himself/itself." PNEUMA's paraphrase ("the One who bore the curse") is essentially the same interpretation.
**Ruling:** "Saved by the Accursed One himself" (LOGOS) adopted as the primary rendering, with a translator note documenting the full range of interpretations.

---

## Disagreement 6 — v.6: formatting the three signs

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | Prose list |
| LOGOS | Structured prose with "first / then / third" |
| PNEUMA | Dramatic fragmented lines ("first — / then — / then —") |

**Issue:** The Greek presents the signs as a numbered list (πρῶτον / εἶτα / τρίτον = first / then / third). LOGOS's structure is clear and formal.
**Ruling:** LOGOS's structured prose adopted. The numbered sequence is preserved.

---

## Disagreement 7 — v.8: "upon the clouds" vs. "on the clouds"

| Agent | Rendering |
|-------|-----------|
| EMET | "coming upon the clouds of heaven" |
| LOGOS | "coming on the clouds of heaven" |
| PNEUMA | "coming on the clouds of heaven" |

**Issue:** ἐπὶ τῶν νεφελῶν = on/upon the clouds. Minor preposition variation.
**Ruling:** "Coming on the clouds of heaven" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) adopted. Standard English idiom matches the parallel in Matt 24:30 and Dan 7:13 (LXX).
